findings.issue: Scratch verification script written to /tmp, where ESM resolution cannot find the repo's @playwright/test, wasting a turn
findings.suggestion: Write throwaway scripts inside the repo (and delete them) so module resolution and cwd are correct

findings.issue: Orphan app process left on port 3200 (from a failed prior run) served stale config pointing at port 9000, causing a misleading 30s test timeout and several diagnosis turns
findings.suggestion: pgrep/kill by pattern before starting any server, and always start probes on fresh ports with a trap-based cleanup

findings.issue: First draft of server/api/team.get.ts had interface mismatches, rewritten wholesale one turn later
findings.suggestion: Draft the shape of the response alongside the composable that consumes it before writing either file

findings.issue: find -exec over possibly-absent dirs exited 1 (one of the 4 bash failures)
findings.suggestion: Use `2>/dev/null || true` or check dirs exist first

findings.issue: Browser verification asserted text content only; never rendered/inspected the team page visually
findings.suggestion: A single screenshot read-back would have confirmed the new team-grid CSS (button placement under cards) looks right

summary: An unusually disciplined 34-turn session: full requirements read up front, a correct SSR-aware design chosen before coding, and the feature passed the entire suite on the first full run with zero fix cycles. It went beyond the tests by reading installed Nuxt source to find and fix a latent client-navigation caching bug, then verified that exact scenario in a real browser and re-ran the full suite after its final edit. The only real waste was ~4 turns fumbling its own ad-hoc server-startup harness for the manual check.

loops.what: Repeatedly failed to get the manual browser check running: script in /tmp couldn't resolve @playwright/test, then an orphan app process on port 3200 served stale API config and timed out the probe
loops.brokenBy: Moved the script into the repo, killed orphan processes by pattern, and re-ran on fresh ports 3201/9201
